title: Psalm 67: Let All the Peoples Praise You
summary: Echoing the priestly blessing, the psalmist asks God to be gracious to his people and make his face shine on them, so that God's ways and salvation will be known among all nations. A refrain calls all peoples to praise God, who judges them justly and guides them. The psalm ends with a harvest gathered and a prayer that God's blessing will lead the ends of the earth to fear him.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 65
from.text: After a long run of laments and trust psalms (51 to 64), it opens a group of four songs of praise (65 to 68) that celebrate God's rule over creation and the nations.

line: A prayer for God to be gracious and make his face shine on his people, so that his salvation will be known among all nations and all peoples praise him.
guide: Ask why you want God's blessing: for your own comfort, or so that others see what he is like. Verse 7 joins the two. Ask who around you could see God's kindness through what he has given you.

stanzas.title: Bless us, so that Your ways may be known on earth
Refrain: let all the peoples praise You
The nations rejoice under God's just rule
Refrain: let all the peoples praise You
Harvest and blessing, so that the ends of the earth fear him

verses.t: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm. A song. May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us, Selah
that Your ways may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples justly and lead the nations of the earth. Selah
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, blesses us.
God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth shall fear Him.
